title: Operator micro-utility hub for safe one-click remediation
creator: Diego Patel
description:
Summary: Build a small, permissioned micro-utility hub in the Operator Console that exposes vetted, reversible 'one-click' remediation actions (e.g., drain node, restart replica, clear cached prefix) as first-class tasks. These utilities should be represented as idempotent Linear-style tasks with auditable inputs, a dry-run mode, and automatic telemetry hooks so support engineers can safely execute common remediations without hand-crafting scripts.

Why: On-call engineers repeatedly perform a small set of manual steps when incidents are transient or well-understood. We want to reduce MTTR, eliminate shell-copying mistakes, and ensure every action is logged, reversible where possible, and tied back to the source of truth (incident ticket or trace).

Scope: MVP exposes 6 safe utilities (drain-instance, soft-restart-service, evict-cache-prefix, rotate-connection-pool, snapshot-and-restart, enable-read-only-mode). Each utility has parameters, a dry-run mode, and a safety pre-check predicate. The hub will: 1) render a compact UI in Console operator view; 2) call an internal admin API (admin-v1) that performs checks, returns a simulated plan for dry-run, and produces an execution log; 3) emit structured telemetry to the Ops dashboard; 4) require RBAC check and optional ephemeral approval for P0 changes.

Design considerations and constraints: actions must be idempotent or transactional where possible; changes must produce clear rollback steps; any action that touches customer data or secrets requires an approval step and audit log entry; integration with KMS for any key rotation operations; we must avoid exposing low-level shell access or arbitrary command execution. The hub will reuse the existing admin-agent service and the runbook-as-task schema but will introduce a compact 'action descriptor' format (name, inputs, safetyLevel, dryRunPlanUrl, rollbackStepsUrl).

Telemetry and observability: each execution produces a trace with action_id, actor, params, dry_run boolean, pre_check results, step-by-step events, and final status. We will add a per-action cost estimate field to help support choose cheaper remediation when available.

Rollout plan: feature-flag behind console.admin.micro_utility_hub; pilot with SRE and Platform Support for two weeks; collect live safety metrics and incidence of manual rollback; expand to wider team after approval.

Non-goals: full orchestration of complex multi-step playbooks, replacing Chaos or automated autorepair engine, or exposing postmortem export UI (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a Micro-Utility hub panel with the 6 listed actions for permitted users
Each action supports dry-run that returns a simulated plan identical in shape to final execution events
Execution requires RBAC check; P0-level actions require ephemeral approval from a second assignee
Every execution creates a structured audit log entry with action_id, actor, inputs, and trace URL
Runbook-as-task representation stored in admin-tasks service and linked back to a Linear ticket
Telemetry appears in Ops dashboard (action count, success rate, avg duration, rollback rate)
steps: Design action descriptor schema and safety predicate (design doc in Confluence)
Add admin API endpoints for dry-run and execute with audit hooks
Define RBAC + ephemeral approval flow and wire to SSO/SCIM
Console UI: compact list, parameter modal, dry-run preview, confirm + run button
Backend: implement 6 MVP actions using adapter layer to operator-agent
Add structured telemetry + dashboard tile and alert for failed rollbacks
Pilot rollout behind feature flag and iterate based on SRE feedback
